sourceContributions.boundary: Source-native rows attached by exact names and identifiers only: an object's own name or host, or one another source states for it (then recorded on the row as `via`). 45,241 cross-identifiers were propagated from attached rows. Aliases are cross-identifiers, not independent confirmation; alternative stellar, transit and microlensing solutions are separate publication rows and are never averaged. Size bound: cross-identifier copies of 30,534 nasa-transiting-planets rows were left out of this release so the file stays within 480,000,000 bytes.

nasa-name-tables.note: keplernames/k2names rows attached as aliases by exact pl_name or KOI designation.

nasa-stellar-hosts.note: Each publication-specific stellarhosts row attaches to every object whose host name, TIC, Gaia DR3, HD or HIP identifier it names exactly (NASA PS planets by host name; TOI, K2 and KOI objects and other catalogs' objects through the identifiers NASA states for them); parameter sets are never merged. The identifiers each row states travel to the object as cross-identifiers.

nasa-transiting-planets.note: TD publication rows attach to the object whose name, or a planet designation another source states for it, is exactly the row's pl_name.

omitted.reason: cross-identifier copies left out to keep the contributions file within 480,000,000 bytes; every row still reaches the object its own name or host attached it to

nasa-microlensing.note: Microlensing solutions (including degenerate models) attach to the object whose name is exactly the row's pl_name; no preferred model is chosen.

nasa-atmospheric-spectroscopy.note: Spectrum metadata rows (type, instrument, wavelength range, reference) attach to the object whose name is exactly the row's pl_name; spectra are not reinterpreted as detections.

nasa-koi-historical.note: q1_q6_koi rows attach to the KOI object with exactly that kepoi_name and to the planet whose name equals the row's kepler_name; each delivery's disposition stays its own row beside the cumulative table's. q1_q8_koi rows attach to the KOI object with exactly that kepoi_name and to the planet whose name equals the row's kepler_name; each delivery's disposition stays its own row beside the cumulative table's. q1_q12_koi rows attach to the KOI object with exactly that kepoi_name and to the planet whose name equals the row's kepler_name; each delivery's disposition stays its own row beside the cumulative table's. q1_q16_koi rows attach to the KOI object with exactly that kepoi_name and to the planet whose name equals the row's kepler_name; each delivery's disposition stays its own row beside the cumulative table's. q1_q17_dr24_koi rows attach to the KOI object with exactly that kepoi_name and to the planet whose name equals the row's kepler_name; each delivery's disposition stays its own row beside the cumulative table's. q1_q17_dr25_koi rows attach to the KOI object with exactly that kepoi_name and to the planet whose name equals the row's kepler_name; each delivery's disposition stays its own row beside the cumulative table's. q1_q17_dr25_sup_koi rows attach to the KOI object with exactly that kepoi_name and to the planet whose name equals the row's kepler_name; each delivery's disposition stays its own row beside the cumulative table's.

nasa-kepler-tce.note: q1_q12_tce rows attach, as a same-star link, to every object whose host is exactly that KIC star (KOI objects and planets NASA names for it); a TCE is a pipeline event, not a planet. q1_q16_tce rows attach, as a same-star link, to every object whose host is exactly that KIC star (KOI objects and planets NASA names for it); a TCE is a pipeline event, not a planet. q1_q17_dr24_tce rows attach, as a same-star link, to every object whose host is exactly that KIC star (KOI objects and planets NASA names for it); a TCE is a pipeline event, not a planet. q1_q17_dr25_tce rows attach, as a same-star link, to every object whose host is exactly that KIC star (KOI objects and planets NASA names for it); a TCE is a pipeline event, not a planet.

exofop.note: Each public ExoFOP TOI row (TFOPWG and TESS dispositions, SG1–SG5 working-group flags, observation counts, comments, update dates) attaches to the TOI object with exactly that designation, to the planet ExoFOP names in Planet Name, and to objects whose host is exactly the row's TIC star (labelled as a same-star link). Dispositions are the provider's; nothing is re-vetted here. Community TOI rows attach to the TOI object the row says it was promoted to, to the planet named in Planet Name, and as a same-star link to objects whose host is exactly the row's TIC star; a community candidate is a submission, not a vetted planet.

vizier.note: SWEET-Cat host rows attach to objects whose host name, or an HD/HIP/TIC/Gaia DR3 identifier stated for the host, equals the catalog's exactly; parameters stay the catalog's own values beside NASA's, never merged. Published prime-mission TOI catalog rows attach to the TOI object with exactly that designation and, as a same-star link, to objects whose host is exactly the row's TIC star; the published vetting is kept beside the rolling NASA/ExoFOP dispositions.

hatnet.note: Each product link the HATNet project declares attaches to the object whose name is exactly the planet named in the file; the link is the project's, the file is not mirrored and its presence is not a new detection.

hatsouth.note: Each product link the HATSouth project declares attaches to the object whose name is exactly the planet named in the file; the link is the project's, the file is not mirrored and its presence is not a new detection.

ads.note: One budgeted ADS query per NASA PS planet (its exact name as a phrase in title or abstract): the record count and the newest records, attached to the object the query named and to objects another NASA table states are that planet; a text match in the literature index is not an identity or confirmation claim. Planets not yet reached by the daily budget have no row.

conflictSets.boundary: Derived build output. One row per source assertion; conflict sets are grouped only after unit, definition, frame, epoch and identity are assessed; selections are versioned choices of source rows (or labelled calculations) beside the rows, never averages and never replacements.

derivedQuantities.claimBoundary: Calculated by WorldsIndex from the values this release selects (a selection, not a measurement) and one stated stellar parameter set. Not a fitted solution, not a self-consistent publication solution and not a completeness-corrected population. Every value names its formula, inputs and their sources.

solarSystemExclusion.rule: Solar System body or interstellar object — not an exoplanet. The host is the Sun (host name "Sun", "Sol", "The Sun" or "Solar System", any case); the object is left out of the atlas and of every product built from it.

scientificBoundary: Static public catalog projection. Source membership is not independent confirmation; source-composite values are not self-consistent publication solutions; catalog projections are not completeness-corrected populations.
